summary: Mazda's P50e plug-in hybrid pairs a 2.5-litre petrol four with a 17.8kWh (gross) battery for 63km of WLTP electric range (76km on Australia's older NEDC claim) and brisk 5.8-second 0-100km/h performance, wrapped in Mazda's most upmarket cabin. A July 2026 repricing cut every P50e grade by $7,150, so the range now runs $56,640 to $76,840 before on-roads across Pure, Evolve, Touring, GT and Azami (plus SP and Takumi packages), and CarExpert calls the cuts 'huge'. Reviewers still rate the interior and safety kit highly, but consistently flag a low-speed transmission that 'stumbles' and shifts roughly even in EV mode, a ride they say may be worse than the petrol and diesel CX-60s, and economics that only work if you charge at home most nights.
pros: July 2026 price cuts of $7,150 per grade put the P50e Pure at $56,640 before on-roads, below a base Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV ES ($58,990), and every grade except the $76,840 Azami SP and Takumi packages sits under the $75,000 FBT cap that applies from April 2027
477L boot with seats up and 1726L seats-down is the same as the petrol and diesel CX-60, so unlike many PHEV rivals the battery pack costs no cargo space (it does cost the spare wheel)
2500kg braked towing capacity matches the inline-six CX-60s and beats most mid-size PHEV SUV rivals, plus a 1500W vehicle-to-load outlet in the boot

5-star ANCAP (2022, tested to Euro NCAP protocols) across the range, front cross-traffic assist and Cruising and Traffic Support now standard on every grade, and an 8-year/160,000km high-voltage battery warranty on top of the 5-year vehicle term
Combined-cycle 49g/km CO2 and 2.1L/100km comfortably qualify every grade for Victoria's green passenger-car duty rate and the higher fuel-efficient LCT threshold
cons: Reviewers describe unresolved drivetrain manners: CarExpert's 2026 GT review says the eight-speed auto 'stumbles' at low speed and the electric drive still produces gearshift sensations in EV mode, a complaint that has persisted since launch

Once the battery is depleted it is a 2.2-tonne petrol AWD SUV using 7.7L/100km on the European charge-sustaining test, against the 2.1L/100km label; CarExpert's 2026 test returned 6.4L/100km, worse than the 5.2L/100km it saw in an Outlander PHEV
Real-world EV range is modest for the price: CarExpert saw 55-60km against the 76km NEDC claim, and its 2026 verdict lists 'EV capability could be better'

PHEVs lost the FBT exemption on 1 April 2025, so the novated-lease case now rests on the fuel-efficient LCT and green duty concessions rather than a tax-free benefit, and the P50e is still $5,000 dearer than the equivalent inline-six grade
The PHEV's ride is the least resolved of the CX-60 range: CarExpert says the extra battery weight leaves it 'messier' over speed bumps and sharp hits than the petrol and diesel versions
